1.note: Interrupter 'of course' needs paired commas; B/D drop one, C semicolon splits a non-clause.

3.note: Next sentence's objection (readers stop buying, authors earn nothing) requires 'reckless'; generous/charitable are near-synonyms so option set partly self-eliminates.

4.note: 'their covers divided into...' is an absolute phrase with no finite verb, so comma is correct; B/C leave a fragment unless 'divided' is misread as an active verb.

5.note: Comma splice fixed by comma + 'but'; C semicolon+and, D 'however' splice.

6.note: Prior sentence 'did not wait for bookshops' sets up 'Instead'.

7.note: Plural subject 'Sales' takes 'were'; past tense of narrative.

8.note: Off-topic shift to Christie's career; D's claim is false per passage, C is the tempting distractor.

9.note: DEFECT: C fixes the dangling modifier but makes the non-underlined 'and passed them along' take 'paperbacks' as subject (paperbacks passed them along); every option leaves the sentence ungrammatical.

10.note: Phrase gives a familiar price comparison for sixpence.

11.note: 'mimic' = imitate; mock/parody imply ridicule, rehearse wrong sense.

12.note: Interrupting color list must be set off by matching dashes.

14.note: 'each' is singular: 'is wired', present tense matches 'can open'.

15.note: Inverted sentence, subject 'two other layers' is plural: 'lie'.

16.note: Taste is irrelevant to color detection; B is the tempting skin-sensor distractor, C's claim is false per paragraph 3.

17.note: Nonrestrictive 'which' clause needs comma; 'that' cannot follow comma.

18.note: Contrast with colorblindness in prior sentence requires 'Even so'.

19.note: Paragraphs 2-3 explain the skin mechanism; D misstates eye content.

20.note: Comma splice fixed by semicolon; C 'although' reverses logic.

21.note: Appositive needs comma; C 'that' after comma wrong, D semicolon before fragment.

22.note: Dismissive register calls for plain 'did only one thing'; feat/wonder/triumph overstate.

23.note: Two independent clauses joined by semicolon; B splice, D run-on, C extra comma.

24.note: Sets up title and paragraph 5 'for forty seconds at a time'.

25.note: Past-tense narration ('cut keys badly', 'would take') requires 'scolded'; stem sentence alone is grammatical.

26.note: Contrasts with 'never scolded': instead of scolding he handed keys back.

28.note: Paragraphs 4-5 show narrator learning what keys mean to customers.

30.note: Neutral 'sign'; omen is future-only/ominous, symptom negative, signal flare absurd.

31.note: Colon introduces explanation after independent clause; B/D leave fragment.

32.note: Measures failing contrasts with efforts described before: 'However'.

33.note: Follows fence/hedge failures and precedes 'Within a season the dirt line would return'.

34.note: Waiting to see where people walk is the opposite of fighting the paths in paragraph 2.

35.note: Run-on fixed with comma + 'and'; D splice, B misused semicolon.

39.note: 'read' = interpret paths carefully; skim/browse contradict 'carefully', proofread wrong sense.

40.note: Essay presents unpaved-lawn waiting as one practice and concedes barriers are sometimes right; not a general argument.
